catalog_quote: A stem may have either one or two syllables. The attested stem-initial syllable shapes are CV, CVC and CCVC ... As for non-initial stem syllables, their only licit shape is CV. Non-initial stem syllables are also restricted with respect to the number of possible consonants, vowels, and tones which they may host. ... the vowel and tone of a non-initial stem syllable can be entirely predicted. ... A non-initial stem syllable can also be said, in phonological parlance, to be unspecified for tone. All of the same tones are available on both monosyllabic and disyllabic stems; the realization of the tone is spread across both syllables when the stem is disyllabic. ... Because of these prominence assymetries between stem-initial and non-initial stem syllables, and despite the lack of any clear phonetic correlate of accent in Mungbam, stem-initial syllables were argued to be accented in Lovegre…

tone_statements.quote: The Munken dialect of Mungbam (ISO mij; Benue-Congo, Cameroon) employs tone lexically and gramatically, contrasting four level tones as well as contours. Noun stems undergo tonal alternations conditioned by the tone of a following possessive pronoun. For some of these alternations it is not obvious that they represent a phonetically natural allophonic process. Furthermore, similar alternations are not observed outside of the possessive construction.

audit.reasoning: The record rests on the standard (and only) reference grammar of Mungbam, Lovegren 2013 (xl+545 pp), which we hold as PDF and text; the deciding quotation is verbatim at sec. 2.1 pp. 23-24 and the tone statements at pp. 42-43, exactly as the locator says. The author's earlier dedicated prosody paper (Lovegren 2012, ACAL 42, open at lingref.com) was downloaded now and states even more explicitly that stem-initial 'accent' is diagnosed solely from contrast-distribution asymmetries with no length, loudness or pitch correlate (pp. 47, 52, 53), confirming the tonal-OR-pitch accent coding with the stem-initial abstract accent noted in the primary-stress rule. The alternative set by morphology (stem-initial) coding remains a defensible judgment call already flagged by a check and B, not a sourcing defect. The only unheld descriptive work is a 2016 Yaounde I MA thesis on the Missong dialect with no online copy; nothin
